audit.whatIsWrong: Last Breath is the tracked, matchup-defining ability across the entire full layer, and nowhere does either layer say that it can only be cast on an AIRBORNE target, or give its cooldown.
audit.why: This is the whole matchup. Last Breath blinks to an Airborne enemy champion — no knockup, no ultimate — and against Ambessa his only self-made knockup is the two-stack Steel Tempest tornado. So 'track Last Breath' is the wrong instruction; the correct instruction is 'do not be standing in the tornado', because denying the trigger removes a 70-second ultimate from the lane entirely without the player ever needing to count it. The cooldown matters at the other end too: it falls to 30 seconds at rank 3, which is why the late-game section is right that he reclaims the lane.
audit.corrected: Last Breath (R), 70/50/30, 1400 range: it blinks only to an AIRBORNE champion. Deny the two-stack Steel Tempest tornado and the ultimate has no trigger.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json — R Last Breath 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion', cd 70/50/30; Q Steel Tempest 'At 2 stacks, Steel Tempest fires a whirlwind that knocks Airborne'

audit.whatIsWrong: Sweeping Blade is described only as an escape on a 'minion cooldown' — 'catch him the instant his E is on minion cooldown', 'save E to dash through the wave and reset distance'.
audit.why: The real restriction is per-target, not per-minion: Sweeping Blade is a 0.5-second cooldown but CANNOT be re-cast on the same enemy for several seconds. Against Ambessa that means the instant he dashes through HER, he is locked out of dashing through her again — the single cleanest pin window in the lane, and it exists whether or not there are minions around. The current wording sends the player to count wave state when the tell is much simpler: he just went through you, so go now.
audit.corrected: Sweeping Blade (E), 0.5s base but locked out on the SAME target for several seconds. The beat right after he dashes through you is your window.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json — E Sweeping Blade: 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds', cd 0.5/0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1

audit.why: The entry's headline interaction is right and well stated: Wind Wall blocks projectiles, and none of Cunning Sweep, Sundering Slam, Repudiation, Lacerate or Public Execution is a projectile, so it does nothing against Ambessa in lane. The content layer already tells the player not to waste tempo baiting it. This is the correct handling of exactly the Wind Wall issue that has been missed elsewhere in this dataset, and I left it intact — only adding Wind Wall's 25s cooldown where it helped.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json — W Wind Wall 'blocks all enemy projectiles', cd 25/23/21/19/17
champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — no projectile flag on any ability

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid credits Ambessa with 'the armor-pen burst'. Steel Tempest is also described as a 'Q double-strike' and a 'tornado windup' without saying what it actually counts as.
audit.why: Public Execution grants no armour penetration in Riot's text — blink, suppress, slam for damage and a stun. The kit file's flags on her R are tooltip-parsing misfires (see notes). Steel Tempest, meanwhile, is 'treated as a basic attack and scales with all the same things', which means it crits, applies on-hit effects, and returns every 4 seconds — that is why his chip beats a single empowered auto in a short trade, and it is also the best thing in his kit to eat with a Repudiation brace.
audit.corrected: Steel Tempest (Q), 4s: counts as a basic attack, so it crits and applies on-hit. Public Execution has no armour penetration — the value is the blink, the suppress and the stun.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json — Q Steel Tempest 'treated as a basic attack and scales with all the same things', cd 4

audit.why: One card would render a Yasuo verdict above text explaining an Ambessa win. Same generator-shaped inversion as several other entries in this file. I did not flip it — chart edits are atomic and mirrored against the Yasuo page — but the prose matches the kit: level 3 is when her Q chain, Lacerate slow and dash all exist against a Sweeping Blade that is locked out on the same target.

notes: This entry already handles the Wind Wall interaction correctly — it explicitly states that none of Ambessa's kit is a projectile, so Wind Wall is a dead button in lane.
